# Transport Contracts Checklist: Search-Service Wiring

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of the CLI + HTTP/SSE transport contract requirements — completeness, clarity, consistency, measurability, and edge-case coverage
**Created**: 2026-09-18
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [data-model.md](../data-model.md) · [contracts/](contracts/ is a directory: cli-search.md, http-search.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are CLI flags specified for every parameter of all five services, including concatenated window flags and regex principal/timeout? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001–FR-010]
- [ ] CHK002 - Are HTTP query parameters specified for the full CLI surface, including which params are route-specific versus shared? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are SSE stream requirements (hit event framing, terminal summary contents, ordering guarantees) fully specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are human-readable CLI output requirements specified, not just `--json` output? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are section-12 contract field requirements enumerated per surface (what lives in CLI JSON vs HTTP data vs HTTP meta)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 - Is canonical-order versus relevance-order behavior disambiguated per tool and per `--explain` value? [Clarity, Spec §US1-AC3]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is clamp-versus-reject behavior specified for each bounded parameter (limit, timeout_ms)? [Clarity, Spec edge cases]
- [ ] CHK008 - Are the default tool (`search_normalized`) and default edition resolution explicitly specified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the CLI↔HTTP parity comparison given an exact basis (which fields, which ordering, which totals)? [Clarity, Spec §SC-002]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK010 - Are CLI flag names and HTTP param names consistently mapped in a documented 1:1 table? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002–FR-010 vs Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK011 - Do error mappings align across surfaces for every failure class (CLI exit code ↔ HTTP status)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012 vs Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK012 - Are profile+rules exclusivity rejections specified identically on both surfaces (exit 2 vs 400, before index access)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, Spec §US3-AC3]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK013 - Can "schema-valid output" be objectively verified — is a concrete schema referenced for each surface? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK014 - Does the misuse matrix cover every rejection case in the FRs (both-present, unknown profile, non-indexed regex field, over-ceiling values)? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is "engine behavior unchanged" given a concrete verification procedure (which suites, which baseline)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is pagination exactness specified with a reproducible procedure (page concatenation equals full ordered set)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK017 - Are empty/whitespace-only normalized query requirements specified for both surfaces (zero hits, never match-all)? [Coverage, Spec edge cases]
- [ ] CHK018 - Are stale-generation drift advisory requirements specified through both surfaces? [Coverage, Spec edge cases]
- [ ] CHK019 - Are SSE client-disconnect and cancellation requirements specified? [Coverage, Spec §US4-AC2]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are unsatisfiable-filter-set requirements specified (zero hits, never error)? [Coverage, Spec edge cases]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK021 - Are over-ceiling limit/timeout requirements specified including effective-value visibility? [Edge Case, Spec edge cases]
- [ ] CHK022 - Are non-loopback bind requirements for the six new routes specified? [Edge Case, Spec edge cases]
- [ ] CHK023 - Are corrupt/stale cache-row requirements specified for both surfaces (miss + recompute, never error)? [Edge Case, Spec edge cases]
- [ ] CHK024 - Are edition-mismatch requirements specified as typed errors rather than silent cross-edition serving? [Edge Case, Spec edge cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK025 - Are per-query timeout budgets specified as requirements on both surfaces (default and ceiling)? [NFR, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK026 - Are regex rate-limit and principal requirements specified on both surfaces? [NFR, Spec §FR-021]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK027 - Are out-of-scope boundaries (engine semantics, CLI tree, read API, normalization catalog, index lifecycle) explicitly excluded? [Dependency, Spec Out-of-scope]
- [ ] CHK028 - Is the stable-service-signatures assumption recorded with a defined fallback if signatures change? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
